messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGING: Elevated 5xx rates observed from customers in private-VPC ingress -> gateway (region-eu1). Automated alert: gateway_5xx_rate > 3% for 5m. Alert details: https://redwood.ops/alerts/1987654321

raj (oncall): seeing lots of 502/504 for private endpoints, started ~12:10 UTC. Confirmed with curl from test-host in same VPC.

laura (support): multiple customers reporting degraded responses, most traffic hitting dedicated private gateway. Customer A reports 20% failures since 11:58.

emily (sre): joining, what's the error from the gateway? logs?

raj (oncall): paste from gateway logs:```
May 03 12:11:03 gateway-01 redwood-proxy[2345]: upstream error: connection reset by peer
May 03 12:11:07 gateway-01 redwood-proxy[2345]: timed out waiting for backend (ctx=snat)
May 03 12:12:10 gateway-02 redwood-proxy[2388]: 502 Bad Gateway
```

sam (netops): I'm running a quick check on NAT ephemeral port exhaustion and SNAT allocation for the affected NAT gateway. Metrics show ephemeral_ports_in_use spiking to > 98% at 12:05 UTC.

raj (oncall): can you run ss -tan and iptables -t nat -L on gateway host?

sam (netops):```
# ss -tan | head
State      Recv-Q Send-Q Local Address:Port               Peer Address:Port
ESTAB      0      0      10.0.5.12:42024                  34.198.12.45:443
ESTAB      0      0      10.0.5.12:42023                  13.224.34.1:443
... (many entries) ...
# iptables -t nat -L -n | grep MASQUERADE
MASQUERADE  all  --  10.0.0.0/16        0.0.0.0/0
```

emily (sre): that SS output and metrics look like SNAT table saturation — ephemeral port space exhausted -> upstream connections failing -> 502/504s. Could be a leak or a bursty pattern causing many short-lived ports. Any recent config changes deployed?

raj (oncall): deploy-bot shows a canary rollout for batch-poller v2 at 11:50 UTC that increases concurrency to backend pool. Noted by deploy-bot:```
deploy-bot: canary rollout: batch-poller v2 -> traffic 30% at 11:50 UTC
```

sam (netops): correlates with spike timestamp. batch-poller might be opening many outbound connections, not reusing keepalives. We should mitigate quickly. Options: 1) increase ephemeral port range on NAT hosts, 2) add additional NAT gateway node (scale out), 3) roll back batch-poller concurrency, 4) enable connection pooling on batch-poller service.

laura (support): customers want ETA. Any immediate mitigation to reduce customer impact?

kyle (infra): I'll spin up an extra NAT gateway in the private subnet and flip routing to add capacity — ~5 min to provision plus health checks. Doing it now.

emily (sre): also suggest short-term firewall tweak: reduce TCP TIME_WAIT reclaim so ports free faster. But risky; prefer scale out + app rollback if needed.

raj (oncall): sam, can you check SNAT conntrack counters and conntrack table size?

sam (netops):```
# conntrack -S
conntrack v1: table size: 65536
entries: 64220
entries/seen: 98.0%
tcp time_wait: 52000
```

sam (netops): conntrack and NAT mapping near capacity. High TIME_WAIT count.

emily (sre): ok, mitigation plan: (A) add NAT gateway node + update route (kyle) (B) temporarily reduce batch-poller concurrency to 5 (raj trigger rollback) (C) monitor 5xx rate and ephemeral ports. If still bad after scale, we do app fix.

raj (oncall): rolling rollback batch-poller concurrency now. Patch in infra pipeline -> patch-id abc123 -> rolling to 100% of canary traffic in 60s.

deploy-bot: rollback initiated: patch abc123 applied to service batch-poller.

kyle (infra): new NAT gateway node provisioned and in service, BGP/route updates applied. Confirming routes:```
# ip route show table nat
default via 10.0.10.2 dev eth0  proto static
192.168.0.0/16 via 10.0.10.3 dev eth1
```

sam (netops): ephemeral_ports_in_use dropping to 45% after NAT scale and rollback. conntrack entries falling.

emily (sre): 5xx rate graphs: https://redwood.monitoring/graph?m=gateways. 5m error rate down from 4.2% -> 0.6% in the last 6m. Good.

laura (support): messaging customers now with initial postmortem and mitigation steps, will update status page.

raj (oncall): keeping thread open for 30m to watch. Will handoff to emily for post-incident follow-up.

emily (sre): taking on post-incident actions: follow-ups: - root cause: SNAT ephemeral port exhaustion caused by increased concurrency from batch-poller v2 canary + insufficient connection reuse - action items: 1) enforce connection pooling in batch-poller, 2) increase conntrack table and ephemeral range on NAT hosts, 3) autoscale NAT gateway earlier on port pressure, 4) add alert for ephemeral_ports_in_use > 80% with immediate paging.

sam (netops): filing infra ticket #INF-3291 for conntrack tuning and autoscale rule.

kyle (infra): will schedule a controlled config change for TIME_WAIT tuning after safety window.

laura (support): customers updated with mitigation note and milestone ETA for permanent fix. No escalations outstanding.

emily (sre): closing incident in 45m if metrics stable. Thanks all for quick turnaround :thumbsup:

incident-bot: incident closed in channel: incidents by emily (sre). Summary: transient NAT/SNAT port exhaustion -> scaled NAT + rollback -> services recovered. Link: https://redwood.incidents/1987654321
